L0_intent: Determine the minimum number of non-adjacent jumps required to solve all problems such that no two consecutive problems have the same tag, or report if it is impossible.

L1_approach.strategy: Check feasibility using the pigeonhole principle. If feasible, compute the cost by analyzing the number of adjacent same-tag pairs, treating the sequence as a path graph where edges are 'free' moves.
L1_approach.complexity: O(n) time, O(n) space per test case

L2_units.name: calc
L2_units.responsibility: Calculates the minimum cost of a valid permutation for a sequence of tags.
L2_units.contract: Takes an array of integers; returns the minimum cost or -1 if no valid permutation exists. Handles single elements and impossible tag distributions.

steps.text: Determine the length of the input array.
Return zero immediately if the array contains only a single element.
Initialize an array to count the frequency of each tag value.
Iterate through the input to populate the tag frequency counts.
Return -1 if any single tag appears more than half the time plus one.
Initialize a penalty array and increment counts for the first and last elements.
Iterate through adjacent pairs and add two to the penalty count if their tags match.
Calculate and return the minimum cost based on the total and maximum penalty counts.

L2_units.name: <main>
L2_units.responsibility: Orchestrates the processing of multiple test cases.
L2_units.contract: Reads stdin, calls the calculation per test case, prints each result.

steps.text: Read the number of test cases from standard input.
Loop through each test case, read the array, convert to zero-based indices, print the result.
